name: shell-hygiene-secrets
description: Blocks the `op` commands that print a secret into the session and need a command path: `op item get --format json`, `op document get`, `op run`, `op inject` and `op signin --raw`, and a secret-printing `op`, `gh` or `security` command run through `nix run`. The shell-hygiene rulebook holds `op read` and `op item --reveal` as version 1 rules, which see past an `op` global option such as `--account my`, and the `gh`, `security` and `secretspec` secret rules, `secretspec run -- op` among them. List `nix` in the config's `transparent_wrappers`, and no other command, so these rules also apply under `nix develop --command` and `nix shell`; `nix run` names its program inside a flake reference, which a wrapper can't see, so it keeps a rule of its own. `secretspec` is not a transparent wrapper, since it runs `op` itself on the agent's behalf. The why and the alternatives live in the shell-hygiene-secrets-through-secretspec skill in nhooey/shell-skills. Known misses, kept as `allowed` fixtures so a fix shows up as a failing test: an `op` global option that takes a value before the subcommand, such as `op --account my item get X --format json` or `op --format json item get X`; `--format=JSON`; and an `OP_FORMAT=json` prefix. Also not caught: a `nix` global option before `run`.
author: nhooey/shell-skills

rules.name: op-item-format
rules.reason: `op item get --format json` prints concealed fields, as do `op item create` and `op item edit` with it. Read the secret through SecretSpec: `secretspec get --reason "…" KEY`. `op item list --format json` still works.

rules.name: op-document-get
rules.reason: Prints a stored document into the session or writes it to a file. Ask the user, or read it through SecretSpec into the one command that needs it.

rules.name: op-run
rules.reason: Loads secrets into a command, and `--no-masking` or any change to a value gets them past its output masking. Use `secretspec run --reason "…" -- <command>`.

rules.name: op-inject
rules.reason: Writes every secret a template names into the session or a file. Read each through SecretSpec into the one command that needs it: `secretspec get --reason "…" KEY`.

rules.name: op-signin-raw
rules.reason: Prints a 1Password session token into the session. Let SecretSpec talk to 1Password.

rules.name: nix-run-secret-read
rules.reason: Runs a secret-printing `op`, `gh` or `security` command through `nix run`, whose program CC Safety Net can't see inside the flake reference. Read the secret through SecretSpec into the one command that needs it.

tests.command: env FOO=1 op item get abc --format json
nix develop --command op item get abc --format json
nix develop -c op item get abc --format json
nix shell nixpkgs#_1password-cli --command op item get abc --format json
nix run nixpkgs#_1password-cli -- item get abc --reveal
op --account my item get abc --format json
